fields.why: Table 1 gives 2014 rates with CIs for 5 race/ethnicity and 5 age groups, and Figure 1 AAPCs for 4 adult age groups are compared ('trends varied substantially by age group').
Sex has 2 levels; Census region and state are geography, not SPDs.

The methods' CI line for 'informal comparisons among rates' sits under 'higher' claims across race and age groups, which v5.2 maps to per-group vs referent only (side by side is the alternative if the line is not read as an overlap rule). The AAPC entry is side by side: each AAPC is tested only against zero (rule 6), and Figure 1 has no CIs, so the mechanical flag is a false alarm.

brief_issues: A methods line that offers CIs 'for informal comparisons ... without specifying a referent group' is not clearly an overlap significance rule; the brief could say whether it triggers per-group vs referent only.
